Name: Little's Law
Inputs: λ = arrival rate (req/s); W = avg time in system (s)
Rule of Thumb: Use to size thread pools and connection pools
Gotcha: Only valid for stable systems (arrival rate ≤ service rate); doesn't account for bursts

Name: QPS from Daily Active Users
Inputs: DAU; actions per user per day; peak factor (typically 2-5x)
Example Calculation: 10M DAU × 10 actions / 86400 = ~1157 QPS avg; ~3472 QPS peak (3x)
Rule of Thumb: Peak is typically 2-5x average; use 3x as default unless you have data
Gotcha: Weekend vs weekday patterns can vary 10x for some apps; don't use a single peak factor

Name: Storage Estimation
Inputs: Row count; avg row size in bytes; replication factor
Rule of Thumb: Add 30% overhead for indexes; double for 2-year growth
Gotcha: Compression ratios vary wildly (2x-10x); always measure with real data

Name: Bandwidth Estimation
Rule of Thumb: Multiply by 2 for bidirectional; add 20% for protocol overhead
Gotcha: Payload sizes vary per endpoint; use P95 not average for capacity planning

Name: USL (Universal Scalability Law)
Inputs: N = nodes; α = contention; β = coherency
Rule of Thumb: If β > 0 the system has a maximum useful parallelism; adding more nodes degrades performance
Gotcha: β (coherency) is the killer — even tiny values cause retrograde scaling at high N

Name: Amdahl's Law
Inputs: p = parallelizable fraction; N = number of processors
Rule of Thumb: Even 5% serial work limits max speedup to 20x regardless of cores
Gotcha: Applies to any parallelization — threads; shards; replicas; not just CPUs

Name: Connection Pool Sizing
Inputs: QPS; avg query latency; connections per request; headroom factor
Gotcha: Too large pools cause contention on the DB side; PostgreSQL recommends max_connections < 200 per instance

Name: Kafka Partition Sizing
Inputs: Target throughput (MB/s); per-partition throughput; desired consumer parallelism
Example Calculation: 100 MB/s target / 1 MB/s per partition = 100 partitions
Rule of Thumb: 1 partition ≈ 1 MB/s producer throughput; 1 consumer per partition
Gotcha: Over-partitioning increases end-to-end latency and metadata overhead; Kafka recommends < 4000 partitions per broker

Name: Cache Size Estimation
Inputs: Working set cardinality; average object size; memory overhead
Rule of Thumb: Redis uses ~1.5-2x the raw data size due to pointers and metadata
Gotcha: Zipfian distributions mean 10-20% of keys serve 80% of requests; cache the hot set not everything

Name: Disk IOPS Planning
Inputs: QPS; IO operations per query (reads + writes); IOPS per device
Example Calculation: 5000 QPS × 4 IOs/query = 20K IOPS; need 2 NVMe SSDs (each ~10K random IOPS usable)
Rule of Thumb: NVMe: 100K-500K IOPS; SATA SSD: 10K-75K IOPS; HDD: 100-200 IOPS
Gotcha: Advertised IOPS are sequential; random IOPS are 10-100x lower; always benchmark your workload

Name: Replication Bandwidth
Example Calculation: 50 MB/s writes × 2 followers = 100 MB/s replication traffic
Rule of Thumb: Cross-AZ replication adds ~1ms latency per hop; cross-region adds 50-150ms
Gotcha: Synchronous replication doubles write latency; async risks data loss on failover

Name: Fanout Estimation
Inputs: Posts per day; average follower count; fanout-on-write vs read
Rule of Thumb: Fanout-on-write is O(followers) per post; fanout-on-read is O(followees) per read
Gotcha: Hybrid approach: fanout-on-write for users with < 10K followers; fanout-on-read for celebrities

Name: SLO Error Budget
Example Calculation: 99.9% SLO over 30 days = 43.2 minutes of allowed downtime
Gotcha: Partial degradation (slow responses) also consumes error budget; define SLIs precisely

Name: Memory Bandwidth
Inputs: Memory frequency; bus width (typically 64 bits); number of channels
Rule of Thumb: Modern servers: 200-400 GB/s aggregate memory bandwidth; but latency is ~100ns
Gotcha: NUMA effects can halve effective bandwidth for remote memory access

Name: TCP Connection Capacity
Inputs: Ephemeral port range (default ~28K on Linux); unique destination IP:port pairs
Rule of Thumb: Linux default ephemeral range: 32768-60999 (28232 ports); increase with sysctl
Gotcha: TIME_WAIT sockets consume ports for 60s; high-churn connections exhaust ports quickly
